input.summary:
Full source-fidelity preflight (v10-functional-surface-geometry) completed against input/disclosure.md and the single USER passage in input/conversation.md (which is a truncated duplicate of the disclosure, ending mid-sentence at "The difference between"; input/brief.md was used only for formalities: title, no priority claim, no government support, apparatus + method claims, no means-plus-function, and the preserved terminology list rail / fixed fence / guide carriage / drill bushing / clamp knob / clamping shoe / spacer plate / pointer / center index / sight notch, all of which appear in the text). A complete ledger was built and every item traced to an exact affirmative inventor passage.

Claims: all 22 were traced limitation by limitation. Claim 1 (rail with flat lower face, upper face, longitudinal slot through the rail, distance marks alongside the slot; fence releasably secured at the first end by two screws in two corresponding holes, perpendicular, downwardly projecting portion, first/second orientation by removal-inversion-reinstallation moving the portion between opposite longitudinal sides with the marked face still outward; two separate carriages with key in slot preventing rotation while permitting sliding, one cylindrical bushing per carriage with a bore passing completely through and registering with the slot, clamp knob above the rail with a threaded shank through the carriage and slot into a clamping shoe below, bores parallel and perpendicular to the flat lower face, a pointer per carriage aligned with its bore axis and readable against the marks) maps sentence for sentence onto the disclosure. Dependent claims 2 (separate/uncoupled, independently positionable and clampable), 3 (difference of readings = center-to-center spacing), 4-6 (transverse center index at midpoint, shallow V-shaped sight notch in the second end aligned with it, spaced apart and alignable with the marked centerline), 7 (removable spacer plate with parallel faces, setback changed by its thickness without changing separation), 8 (marks read in the same direction in both fence orientations), 9/17 (hardened-metal replaceable wear-part bushings withdrawable from the carriage body), 10 (rigid polymer or metal parts list, a subset of the disclosed list), 11/22 (no motor, battery, electronic sensor, or network connection; hand-held), 12 (shoe below the lower face, bearing/released), 13-16 (fixed fence not slidable, centering features, reversibility), and method claims 18-21 all trace to affirmative disclosure sentences, including the disclosed use sequence (select spacing, loosen, slide to a difference centered about the index, tighten, place, press fence or spacer plate to the edge, align notch and index to the pencil centerline, drill both bushings, lift away with nothing remaining attached). No means-plus-function language; antecedent basis checked throughout.

Numerals: all 27 entries (10, 12, 14, 16, 18, 24, 26, 30, 32, 34, 36, 40, 50, 52, 54, 58, 60, 62, 70, 72, 74, 78, 80, 82, 90, 92, 94) denote exactly one part each, are used consistently in the description, claims and abstract, and each appears in at least one figure brief; every parenthetical figure citation in the detailed description (14 to FIG. 4; 12, 72, 74, 78, 80 to FIG. 3; 16, 18, 62, 82 to FIG. 2; 52, 54, 58, 60 to FIG. 5; 34, 36 to FIG. 6; 24, 26, 94 to FIG. 7) matches that figure's numeral list.

Figures: the seven briefs depict only disclosed structure. Generic outlines (plain block carriages, plain rectangular fence, plain round body above each carriage, flat-panel workpiece) are declared "shown schematically", the claims and description are shape-neutral about them, and no proportion, count, material, contact, taper, depth, or end-position relationship beyond the disclosure is verbalized. The functional geometry that is stated - the shallow V-shaped notch formed in the second end, the transverse index mark at the midpoint, the key depending into the slot, the shank passing through the slot into the shoe below, the bore passing completely through and aligned with the slot, the spacer plate's two parallel faces bearing on the projecting portion and on the workpiece edge - is affirmatively disclosed verbatim. Section-line designations are consistent in all three places: line 3-3 in the FIG. 2 brief (both endpoints designated 3) matches "FIG. 3 is a cross-sectional view taken on line 3-3 of FIG. 2" in the Brief Description and the detailed description's section through the second guide carriage 70; line 5-5 likewise matches FIG. 5 through the first guide carriage 50.

Text checks: claims and description use the same relationships and terms (downwardly projecting portion, mounting holes, transverse center index, sight notch, clamping shoe, guide carriage); no "by way of example", "any closed outline", or other embodiment-broadening statement was added to the application text to justify a schematic choice; the schematic conventions stay confined to the figure briefs; and no drafting note, placeholder, open question, instruction, unresolved alternative, or internal comment remains. Background prior-art characterizations were not scored for inventor support, per instruction. No unsupported technical assertion and no verified internal inconsistency was found.
